definitions.explanation: The head carpenter who leads a construction project, supervising and coordinating the work of other carpenters. A title of skill and authority in the traditional building trades.
By extension, a leader or head of a group. Used historically for clan leaders and heads of organizations.

examples.japanese: {棟梁|とうりょう}の{指示|しじ}に{従|したが}う。
examples.english: I follow the master carpenter's instructions.

examples.japanese: うちの{家|いえ}を{建|た}てた{棟梁|とうりょう}は{腕|うで}がいい。
examples.english: The master carpenter who built our house is very skilled.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{大工|だいく}たちは{棟梁|とうりょう}のもとで{技|わざ}を{磨|みが}いている。
examples.english: The young carpenters are honing their skills under the master carpenter.

examples.japanese: {一門|いちもん}の{棟梁|とうりょう}として{皆|みな}をまとめた。
examples.english: He brought everyone together as the leader of the group.

examples.japanese: {源氏|げんじ}の{棟梁|とうりょう}として{兵|へい}を{率|ひき}いた。
examples.english: He led troops as the head of the Minamoto clan.

examples.japanese: {武家|ぶけ}の{棟梁|とうりょう}は{強|つよ}い{統率力|とうそつりょく}を{求|もと}められた。
examples.english: The head of a warrior house was required to have strong leadership.

notes:
USAGE:
In modern usage, sense 1 (master carpenter) is most common. When someone says {棟梁|とうりょう} today, they typically mean the head carpenter on a construction project. The word carries a sense of traditional craftsmanship and authority. Sense 2 (leader) is mainly encountered in historical contexts, particularly in reference to the heads of warrior clans during the medieval period.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大工|だいく}の{棟梁|とうりょう}: master carpenter
- {棟梁|とうりょう}の{腕|うで}: the master carpenter's skill
- {武家|ぶけ}の{棟梁|とうりょう}: head of a warrior house
